title: Addition & Result: furthermore, moreover, therefore, as a result
grammarTitle: Addition and Result Markers — Adding and Consequencing
grammarNote: Маркеры добавления (addition) присоединяют новые доводы к уже сказанному. Маркеры результата (result/consequence) показывают, что одна идея является следствием другой. Важно понимать разницу: "furthermore" просто добавляет, а "therefore" утверждает причинно-следственную связь. Неправильный выбор ослабляет аргумент.

grammarTable.subject: furthermore
grammarTable.example: "The policy is expensive. Furthermore, it has not been proven effective."

grammarTable.subject: moreover
grammarTable.example: "The policy is expensive. Moreover, it actively harms the most vulnerable."

grammarTable.subject: in addition
grammarTable.example: "In addition, studies show that..." / "...in addition to its cost..."

grammarTable.subject: therefore
grammarTable.example: "The data supports the hypothesis. Therefore, the model is valid."

grammarTable.subject: as a result
grammarTable.example: "The factory was closed. As a result, 200 workers lost their jobs."

grammarTable.subject: thus
grammarTable.example: "The evidence is strong, thus supporting the conclusion." (can join clauses)

grammarTable.subject: hence
grammarTable.example: "The cost is high, hence the government's reluctance." (literary/academic)

rows.example: "IN ADDITION, the study found..." ✅ — simple addition, no special emphasis.
"FURTHERMORE, this approach also reduces costs." ✅ — a related additional point.
"MOREOVER, the problem is worsening." ✅ — implies the new point is even more significant.
"The policy is expensive. It is ALSO ineffective." ✅ — can be mid-sentence, less formal.

grammarExtra.title: Result markers — different levels of claim

rows.example: "All mammals breathe air. Dolphins are mammals. THEREFORE, dolphins breathe air." ✅
"The factory was closed. AS A RESULT, workers were unemployed." ✅ (cause and effect)
"Temperatures increased. CONSEQUENTLY, sea levels rose." ✅ (more formal than "as a result")
"Data was collected from three sources, THUS ensuring reliability." ✅ (often mid-sentence)
"Furthermore, the data shows..." / "As a result, the policy was changed." ✅
"The policy failed, thus reinforcing the need for reform." ✅ (thus/hence can be mid-clause)
✗ "It was expensive, furthermore it was ineffective." → need semicolon or period: "...; furthermore, it was..."

grammarExtra.title: ⚠️ The critical difference: therefore vs furthermore

rows.example: "All evidence supports the theory. THEREFORE, the theory is correct." — claims logical consequence.
"The policy is expensive. FURTHERMORE, it has not worked." — just adds a second criticism.
✗ "The café was closed. Therefore, I went to the library." → ✅ "AS A RESULT, I went to the library." ("therefore" for pure consequences feels too formal)
Ask: "Does A logically PROVE B?" If yes → "therefore." If A merely CAUSED B → "as a result." If A is just ADDED → "furthermore."

grammarTip:
Addition vs Result — ключевые различия:

ADDITION (добавление):
In addition / Furthermore / Moreover
→ просто добавляют новую мысль
"The policy is expensive. FURTHERMORE, it hasn't worked."

RESULT (следствие/результат):
Therefore / As a result / Consequently / Thus
→ утверждают, что одно вызвало/следует из другого
"Prices rose. AS A RESULT, fewer people bought cars."

⚠️ THEREFORE = логическое следствие (A доказывает B)
AS A RESULT = причинно-следственная связь (A вызвало B)
FURTHERMORE = просто дополнение (ещё один довод)

💡 Запомни: если A не ВЫЗЫВАЕТ B, не используй
"therefore" → используй "furthermore" или "as a result"

exercises.text: "The new software is faster. ___, it uses less memory."
exercises.hint: "FURTHERMORE, it uses less memory." — adding a second benefit. NOT cause-effect. ✅

exercises.text: "The factory was shut down. ___, 500 workers lost their jobs."
exercises.hint: "AS A RESULT, 500 workers lost their jobs." — the shutdown CAUSED the job losses. ✅ Result/consequence.

exercises.text: "The evidence is strong. ___, we can accept the hypothesis."
exercises.hint: "THEREFORE" = logical consequence. The evidence logically supports the hypothesis. ✅

exercises.text: "The experiment failed. ___, it wasted three months of work."
exercises.hint: "MOREOVER" implies the new point is even more significant. "Moreover, it wasted three months" — adds even more impact. ✅

exercises.text: "Prices rose. Therefore, I was unhappy." — "therefore" is correctly used here.
exercises.hint: "Therefore" claims logical causation. Being unhappy about price rises is a natural reaction, not a logical proof. ✅ "As a result, I was unhappy." sounds more natural here.

exercises.text: "CO₂ traps heat. ___, global temperatures are rising."
exercises.hint: "CO₂ traps heat → THEREFORE temperatures rise" (logical consequence ✅) / "AS A RESULT temperatures rise" (causal consequence ✅). Both are natural here!

exercises.text: "The dam was built upstream. ___, the river level dropped."
exercises.hint: "CONSEQUENTLY" = formal result/consequence. The dam caused the river to drop. ✅

exercises.text: "It is expensive, furthermore it is unreliable." — Is this correct?
opts: No — should be "It is expensive; furthermore, it is unreliable."
exercises.correct: No — should be "It is expensive; furthermore, it is unreliable."
exercises.hint: ✅ Use a semicolon or period before "furthermore," not just a comma. "It is expensive; FURTHERMORE, it is unreliable." ✅

exercises.text: "The report found three problems. ___, it suggested five solutions."
exercises.hint: "IN ADDITION, it suggested five solutions." — adding a further fact (solutions), not a result. ✅

exercises.text: "Temperatures have risen. ___, sea levels are higher than fifty years ago."
exercises.hint: "AS A RESULT / CONSEQUENTLY" — higher temperatures cause sea levels to rise. ✅

exercises.text: "Data was collected from five sources, ___ increasing the study's reliability."
exercises.hint: "THUS" can join clauses mid-sentence. "...five sources, THUS increasing reliability." ✅ (academic, formal, mid-sentence)

exercises.instruction: Choose the most formal result marker.
exercises.text: "Emissions increased; ___, climate projections were revised upwards."
exercises.hint: "HENCE" is very formal and academic. "Emissions increased; HENCE, projections were revised." ✅ Most formal option.

questions.hint: "Furthermore" = adds a further point. ADDITION marker. ✅
"Therefore" = the logical consequence of what was just said. RESULT marker. ✅

opts: "Moreover" is more emphatic — new point is even more significant
questions.correct: "Moreover" is more emphatic — new point is even more significant
questions.hint: "Moreover" suggests the new point is even more important than the previous. ✅

questions.text: "The lab was flooded. ___, the experiment was delayed."
questions.hint: Cause and effect → "AS A RESULT / CONSEQUENTLY." The flooding caused the delay. ✅
"Prices rose → THEREFORE consumers spent less." = logical cause and effect. ✅

questions.text: When should you use "therefore" not "as a result"?
questions.hint: "Therefore" = logical proof (A proves B). "As a result" = cause-effect (A caused B). ✅ Overlap but different nuances.

questions.text: "The policy was unpopular. Furthermore, it was expensive." — "furthermore" is:
questions.hint: "Furthermore" adds a second point (expensive) to the first (unpopular). ADDITION. ✅

opts: Only at the start of sentences
Mid-sentence to join clauses; very formal/academic
questions.correct: Mid-sentence to join clauses; very formal/academic
questions.hint: "THUS" is academic/formal and can appear mid-clause. "Data was collected, THUS ensuring reliability." ✅

questions.text: "It is expensive, furthermore it is unreliable." — What is wrong?
opts: "Furthermore" needs a semicolon/period before it, not just a comma
questions.correct: "Furthermore" needs a semicolon/period before it, not just a comma
questions.hint: ✅ "It is expensive; FURTHERMORE, it is unreliable." — comma alone creates a comma splice. ✅
"Consequently" is more formal and academic than "as a result." Both signal consequence. ✅

questions.text: "The experiment was successful. ___, the team celebrated."
questions.hint: All three work: "AS A RESULT" / "THEREFORE" / "CONSEQUENTLY" — the success caused/led to celebrating. ✅

questions.text: "In addition" is most similar in meaning to:
questions.hint: "In addition" ≈ "furthermore" — both ADD a new point. "In addition" is slightly more neutral. ✅

opts: "The policy failed. Moreover, it was a success."
"Prices rose. Furthermore, fewer people could afford cars."
"The water was cold. As a result, it tasted nice."
questions.correct: "Prices rose. Furthermore, fewer people could afford cars."
questions.hint: Rising prices → fewer can afford cars: related addition. ✅ Others use wrong linkers for the logic.
"HENCE" = formal/literary. Similar to "therefore." "The cost is high, hence the hesitation." ✅

questions.text: "All mammals breathe air. Dolphins are mammals. ___, dolphins breathe air."
questions.hint: "THEREFORE" = logical deduction/proof. This is classic syllogism — logical proof, not just cause-effect. ✅

questions.text: Which linker would NOT work in this sentence: "The report was delayed. ___, the meeting was postponed."
questions.hint: "FURTHERMORE" adds a new unrelated point — but postponing a meeting IS the result of the delay. ✅ "Furthermore" signals addition, not result. "Therefore/As a result/Consequently" would all work.
